topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and frames its conceptual importance and complexity.

topics.label: Complement system principles and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core architecture, naming conventions, and central functional role of C3 in complement biology.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms of the alternative, lectin, and classical pathways that trigger complement activation on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary effector functions carried out by activated complement components to clear pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how regulatory proteins inhibit complement cascade progression to protect host tissues from damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical presentations and disease phenotypes arising from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the strategies evolved by pathogens to resist complement activation and clearance.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture and previews the next topic in the lecture series.
